_comment: The screenshot carousel's data. Adding a shot to the site is three steps and no code:
1. drop the PNG in Screenshots/ at the repo root,
2. add an entry here (source = its filename, id = the web asset's basename),
3. run `npm run screenshots:build && npm run build:site`.
and <id>-1600.webp; scripts/build-site.ts reads this file and generates the slides, the
captions and the progress segments from it. The carousel script never names an image.
Order here is the order on the page.
Screenshots/ holds exactly the eight sources this file lists, and they are committed,
so `npm run screenshots:build` needs no argument and reproduces the .webp set byte
for byte. Two captures were removed rather than left lying unused:
live capture.png was a 551x148 crop of the clipboard toast; the frame is 3:2, so it
would have been upscaled ~3x beside the 2544x1644 shots. Re-shoot it full-window if
the clipboard watcher deserves a slide.
unsupported links.png showed an engine error. It was on the page briefly and Isaac
asked for it off: a red ERROR block is not what a landing page should lead with.

shots.title: Paste a link, pick a quality
shots.caption: One field takes a video, a playlist or a live stream. Nothing is downloaded until you have seen what the link actually is.
shots.alt: StreamDock's Capture tab with an empty URL field, a Video and Stream toggle, and a quality selector beside the Download button.

shots.title: Analyze before you download
shots.caption: StreamDock probes the link first — what it is, how many items it holds, and which audio and subtitle tracks the source really offers.
shots.alt: The Capture tab with an anime episode URL pasted into the field, ready to analyze.

shots.title: Playlists, understood
shots.caption: Every item comes back with its real title, thumbnail and length. Take all of it, the first few, a range, or schedule it for later.
shots.alt: A YouTube playlist of fifteen networking videos analyzed in StreamDock, each row showing a thumbnail, title, duration and checkbox, next to All, First N, Range and Schedule options.

shots.title: A queue you can steer
shots.caption: Live speed and time remaining on every row, pause or cancel any of them, and a details panel carrying the engine's own output when something goes wrong.
shots.alt: StreamDock's Downloads tab with one episode running at 28 percent showing 1.49 MB per second, and a second episode queued behind it.

shots.title: Finished, and easy to find
shots.caption: Completed files keep the title the source gave them — no invented episode numbering — with Open and Folder right there on the row.
shots.alt: The Downloads tab showing one completed 222 MB episode with Open, Folder and Remove buttons, and a second episode still downloading at 52 percent.

shots.title: Engines already bundled
shots.caption: yt-dlp and ffmpeg ship inside the app and report ready on launch. Set the save folder, concurrency and clipboard watcher once and forget them.
shots.alt: StreamDock's Settings tab showing an Engines ready badge, the save location, concurrency slider, clipboard URL watcher, and advanced yt-dlp options.

shots.title: Twelve ambient themes
shots.caption: Match the app to this site's gradient, pick one of the twelve themes, pull a fresh photo on a schedule, or drop in a flat colour.
shots.alt: The Advanced Background panel showing a grid of twelve ambient theme swatches and a live wallpaper preview with a refresh interval.

shots.title: Make it yours
shots.caption: Whatever background you choose sits behind every screen, with the chrome staying readable on top of it.
shots.alt: StreamDock's Capture tab rendered over a mountain landscape wallpaper, its panels still legible against the photo.
